about: The saved-measurement library: importing, editing and saving, and the message an import shows. Each case starts with an empty library and a fresh analyzer and runs its 'steps' in order: {"import": [names]} imports one .guitartap file holding those measurements (the 'measurements' entries), through the app's import (importAndLoadMeasurements — a single measurement is also loaded); {"edit": {entry, name, notes}} edits the library's entry at that position as the Edit sheet does; {"save": name} saves the result on screen under that name; {"deleteAll": true} deletes every saved measurement, as Delete All does; {"warning": text} puts up a microphone warning, as an earlier load would. 'expect' after the last step: 'library' (the entries' names, in order), 'notes' (their notes, null for none), 'persisted' (the names read back from storage — the natives' file, the web's IndexedDB), 'ids' (each entry's id: a measurement's name for that file's own id, 'new' for one minted since), 'message' / 'messageStartsWith' (the last import's message), 'microphoneWarning' (a warning is up), 'exportHasRowKey' (an exported file carries the library's row key). 'only' marks a case about something one side alone has ('natives' or 'web'). Expected values are Swift's.

cases.note: importing a file adds its measurement to the library, saved, with the file's own id
importing the same file again appends a second entry; both keep the file's id
a file of two measurements adds both, in order
editing an entry changes only that entry, in its place, and gives it a new id (amended data is a different dataset)
editing one of two duplicate imports leaves the other, which keeps the shared id
a save appends after the entries already there
editing an entry that is not there changes nothing (the natives address entries by position; the web by row key)
the library's row key never reaches an exported file (only the web's library has row keys)
Delete All empties the library and its saved copy
a library import says nothing about microphones, even ones that are not connected

steps.warning: a warning from an earlier load

cases.note: a single-file import carries the load's microphone warning in its one message, so no second warning shows
